cultural.vision_reason: The image shows a wooden animal mask with formline painted designs, protruding tongue, and hide ear flap — a classic Northwest Coast ceremonial mask consistent with Haida (or closely related Northwest Coast) carving traditions.

physical.title: mask
physical.summary: Mask made of wood depicting an animal. The face has a prominent snout, wide eyes, open mouth and protruding tounge. Three orifices surround the tounge within the mouth. The mask is painted in red, green and black pigments, with the red on the tounge and lips, black on the eyes and green framing the face. To the right of the face there is a hide flap, possibly depicting an ear, with formline designs in black and red pigment. The strap is attached to the mask with sinew and a hide cord runs from the top of the rear of the mask, ending in a knot. This would have originally helped hold the mask to the wearer's face. The entire mask shows signs of extensive historic burrowing insect activity, which probably occurred pre-collection: much of the nose is missing, as is the left ear flap and most of the top and left hand side of the green border.
